   President Trump at a rally groused about how Fox News handled El-Sayed during an interview.

   “El-Sayed was interviewed just a little while ago on a certain network…They let this guy talk, talk, talk. They hardly fight him at all. Why are they putting these people on our television networks?”

   Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez   (D., N.Y.) , during a private event in New York, was absolutely gushing about what happens if El-Sayed wins.

   “What we do is that we break open the entire political calculus in America—period,” Ocasio-Cortez said, according to the New York Times . “Because if you can win, if Abdul can win in Michigan, anybody can win anywhere. Anywhere.”

   Former President Barack Obama announced he was headed to Michigan later this month to campaign with El-Sayed. This brings the Democratic seal of approval onto a candidate that didn’t have support from many in the Democratic establishment during his primary battle against Rep. Haley Stevens. El-Sayed Has Trump Fuming, AOC Buzzing and Obama Stumping
 
Plus, Scott Bessent has a lot on his plate, and U.S. escalates pressure on Russia over lab death in Siberia
 
 
SARAH RICE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

Good morning. Abdul El-Sayed BARELY won the Democratic primary in Michigan just two months ago. Now he’s drawing a ton of attention from the top leaders in both parties with less than a month to go in a U.S. Senate race that he…just…might…win.

 

He went from being seen as a potential anvil for the Democrats to a game-changer within the party.

 

Look at just the attention he drew JUST SINCE MONDAY:

 

President Trump at a rally groused about how Fox News handled El-Sayed during an interview.

 

“El-Sayed was interviewed just a little while ago on a certain network…They let this guy talk, talk, talk. They hardly fight him at all. Why are they putting these people on our television networks?”

 

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D., N.Y.), during a private event in New York, was absolutely gushing about what happens if El-Sayed wins.

 

“What we do is that we break open the entire political calculus in America—period,” Ocasio-Cortez said, according to the New York Times. “Because if you can win, if Abdul can win in Michigan, anybody can win anywhere. Anywhere.”

 

Former President Barack Obama announced he was headed to Michigan later this month to campaign with El-Sayed. This brings the Democratic seal of approval onto a candidate that didn’t have support from many in the Democratic establishment during his primary battle against Rep. Haley Stevens. Former Vice President Kamala Harris has already campaigned with El-Sayed, and now he’ll have Obama by his side as well.

 

This is an edition of the Politics newsletter, bringing you an expert guide to what’s driving D.C. every day. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

People and Policies I’m Watching

 

Max Miller: The embattled Republican congressman is betting voters in his Ohio district have heard about his domestic-violence allegations, and he is leaning in.

 

Trump’s Wednesday: The president is scheduled to hold policy meetings at 10 a.m. ET and 12:30 p.m. He will make an announcement at 1 p.m., and will later depart for San Antonio, where he is set to deliver remarks at a midterm rally in the evening.

What I’m Following

 
 
EDUARDO MUNOZ ALVAREZ/GETTY IMAGES
 

The Treasury secretary has a lot on his plate—and it is beginning to show. Scott Bessent is facing intense pressure from Trump to tame the markets, end the war in Iran and boost the economy—and the pressure is weighing on him, according to people close to him. The Treasury secretary is increasingly lashing out at his own staff and making unusual market interventions, alienating even some of his own allies.

 

Marco Rubio tries to calm Iceland’s fears over Trump’s territorial ambitions for the Arctic. The secretary of state visited Iceland on Tuesday, seeking to turn the president’s controversial push to take control of Greenland into an effort to expand U.S. military reach across the region. His trip came after Trump’s Greenland campaign rattled Reykjavík, which recently summoned the U.S. ambassador over a White House post depicting Iceland under an American flag.

 

The U.S. escalates pressure on Russia over a Siberia lab death. Washington has warned Moscow that its failure to disclose details about the death of a lab worker from a plague-research center runs counter to its international health obligations, U.S. officials said. The mysterious episode has stirred fears that an infectious disease might spread inside Russia and beyond the country’s borders.

 
 
 

What Else Is Happening

 

• A WSJ reporter went back to Idaho to see how the hard-right transformed this deep red state.

 

• U.S. sanctions on alleged cartel-linked officials infuriated Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum as she faces pressure from the Trump administration.

 

• The U.S. trade deficit widened in August to its biggest in more than a year.
